2-101 Adoption of state rules and regulation.

The rules and regulations promulgated by the State Election Board which pertain to municipal elections, together with the provisions of the Georgia Municipal Election Code contained in Title 34A of the Georgia Code Annotated, are hereby adopted as the rules, regulat~ fons and provisions that shall govern the conduct of municipal general and special elections in this city.

a :

NOTE: Authority to adopt state rules and regulations in this area is conferred on municipalities by the Municipal Election Code. See Georgia Code Annotated. 34-201.

2-102 Expenses.

Such funds as are necessary for the conduct of elections and for the performance of the duties that are specified by this chapter shall be budgeted and appropriated annually, and from time to time.

NOTE: Municipalities are required by law to budget funds

CO for the conduct of municipal elections. See Ga. Code Ann. 34-201.

2-201 Registrars and deputy registrars.

- 1. Appointment. Registrars and deputy registrars shall

. be appointed by the Mayor and Council, as necessary, and shall serve at the pleasure of same. One such appointee shall be designated as chief registrar, and such person shall serve as the chief administrative officer of the board of registrars and shall generally supervise and direct the administration of the affairs of said board. :

All appointments shall be entered on the minutes of the council meeting at which they are made.

- 2. Qualifications. Registrars and deputy registrars shall be electors of the municipality ‘and shall be able to read, write and speak the English language. Such appointees, while serving as registrars or deputy registrars or with- in a period of six months after so serving, shall not be eligible to any nomination or office to be voted for at e a primary or election.

- 3. Oath. Prior to entering upon his duties, each registrar and deputy registrar shall swear to faithfully perform his duties, such oath to be administered by an officer authorized by law to administer the oath.

- 4. ‘Term of office. Registrar shall be appointed by the Mayor and Council and shall serve until their successors are appointed and qualified, except in the event of resignation or removal as hereinafter provided.

C) resigns or is removed for cause, his duties and authority as such shall terminate instanter. Each such appointment shall be entered on the minutes of the council meeting at which the appointment is made.

2-202 Elector qualifications.

Any person desiring to vote in any municipal general or special election must (1) register as an elector at least 15 days prior to the primary or election at which he desires to vote fbut see NOTE); (2) be’a citizen of the State of Georgia and of the United States; (3) be at least eighteen years of age and (4) be a resident of this municipality.

NOTE: The specific time limit for registration is determined by charter or ordinance, but must be no longer than 50 days and no shorter than 15 days, unless the municipality elects to utilize the county registration list, in which case a person must register with the county registrar at least 30 days prior to the municipal primary or election.':See 344-507 of the Georgia Code Annotated.

Registration lists and records.

The City shall maintain its own registration system (but see NOTE). The form of the registration cards shall conform to the provisions of section 34-609 of the Georgia Code Annotated. The completed registration cards and other papers of the registrars shall be kept in the main office of the board of registrars in City Hall and shall be open to public inspection during usual business hours.

NOTE: The City may elect either to maintain its own regis~ tration system or use the county registration list of eligible voters. See Ga. Code Ann., 34-506.

Permanancy of registration.

Registration of an elector will remain permanent if the elector votes in at least one election every three years. If such person does not vote in at least one general or special election or primary in a three-year period and does not specially request continuation of his registration, then the elector's , name will be removed from the registration list and le shall be required to reregister in the manner provided for original registration. .

Absentee registration.

Absentee registration shall not be allowed in any municipal primary or general or special election held in the city.

NOTE: This is a requirement of state law. See Ga. Code Ann. | 34A-513.

Notice of candidacy.

- i. Filing. Each candidate desiring to have his name placed on the ballot for an office to be filled ina municipal general or special election shall file personally, or by his agent, notice of his candidacy in the manner and accompanied by the documents and information required by section 34A-901 of the Georgia Code Annotated. Such filing shall be made at least fifteen, but not more than forty five days prior to the election in the case of a general election and at least ten, but not more than thirty days prior to the election in the case of a special election.

In the event a runoff primary is held, each candidate . nominated therein, or his agent, shall file notice of his candidacy within three days after the holding of such runoff primary, irrespective of such three day period's exceeding the qualification deadline hereinabove prescribed.

NOTE: The Municipal Charter may require that the notice Of Candidacy be accompanied by a nomination petition, in which case the petition must conform to all charter

. provisions as well as to the requirements of section 34A-910 of the Georgia Code Annotated.

- 2. Designation of office sought. In the event a candidate seeks oné of two or more public offices of the city, each having the same title and to be filled at the same election by the vote of the same electors, such candidate shall not be required to designate the specific office he is seeking; in all such elections the number of candidates equal to the number of such public offices to be filled at the election who receive the greatest

C) number of votes shall be elected.

NOTE: In determining whether a candidate must designate the specific office sought in elections of this kind, charter provisions govern. If the charter is silent, the determination can be made by ordinance.

2-302 Qualification fees.

The qualification fee for candidates filing a notice of candidacy for any office in any general or special election shall be twenty dollars, which fee shall be paid to the municipal superintendent at the time of the filing of such notice of candidacy.

NOTE: Candidate filing fees, even if reasonable, may be subject to federal Constitutional attach on equal protection grounds if payment of the fee is the sole means of access to the ballot. See Jenness v. Little, 306 F. Supp. 925 (1968), Jenness v. Fortsone 315 F. Supp. 1035 (1970); and Bulloch V- Carter, 405 U. 134 (1972).

2-303 Campaign financing disclosure. All candidates for municipal public office shall keep all v) such records and file all such reports as are required by the Georgia Campaign Disclosure Act.

Election districts

The area comprising the corporate limits of the City, as the same is now or shall hereafter exist, shall constitute the sole election district of the City.

NOTE: Subject to prior approval of the United States Attorney General-or the D. C. District Court pursuant to Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, the Mayor and Council may consolidate election districts, or divide any election district into two or more districts of compact or contiguous territory, or alter the bounds of any election district, but any such change must be made at least sixty days before a general election and at least thirty days before a special election. If there is more than one election district within the City, each district should be named and its boundaries delineated in this section.

Polling places.

The polling place within the City shall be the City Hall located at the City Hall Building on Langford Street.

NOTE: Insofar as practicable the polling place selected should be the same as that used in county and state elections, and preferably should be a schoolhouse, municipal building or other public building. If there is more than one election district within the City, then a separate polling place should be designated for each district.

Write-in votes.

Write-in votes shall be permitted in municipal elections, except that no write-in votes shall be counted-in a primary, runoff primary, or runoff election.

NOTE: See Ga. Code Ann. 34A-1124. Absentee ballots.

Absentee ballots shall be used in all municipal elections, and such use shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter 34-A-13 of the Georgia Code Annotated.

NOTE: Municipal governing bodies are authorized to legislate, regulate and administer all matters pertaining to absentee voting in municipal elections. See Ga.’ Code Ann. 69-310.

Vote required for election.

Candidates for nomination for any public municipal office in any primary, and candidates for any public municipal office in any election shall be nominated or elected by a plurality of the votes cast to fill such nomination or public office.

NOTE: The Municipal Election Code requires a majority vote n municipal elections unless the municipality through its charter or by ordinance authorizes a plurality vote. In all cities having a population in excess of 100,000 people, however, a candidate must receive a majority of the votes cast in order to be nominated for or elected to public office. See Ga. Code Ann. 34A-1407.

Contested elections.

- 1. Petition of contest. Any person wishing to contest the results of a primary or election shall file a petition with the city clerk within five days after the results of the election are certified to the Mayor and Council, which petition shall set forth in writing one or more of the following grounds:

- a. Malconduct, fraud or irregularity by any election official sufficient to change or place in doubt the , result.

- b. Ineligibility of the defendant for the office in dispute. .

- c. Illegal votes received, or legal votes rejected, sufficient to change or place in doubt the result.

- d. An error in counting the votes or in declaring the result of an election; if such error would change the result.

- 2. Notice and hearing. Upon the filing of the contest petition, a hearing shall be set before the Mayor and Council and written notice stating the time and place of the hearing and containing a copy of the contest petition shall be given to all affected candidates. The hearing will take place not less than ten (10) nor more than thirty (30) days after service of the notice upon the affected candidates, and shall be conducted in an informal manner. ,

- 3. Determination by Mayor and Council. The Mayor and Council shall examine the qualifications of electors con-~ cerning their right to vote, order a recount of ballots, examine the registration lists and perform such acts and conduct such examinations as may be deemed necessary to determine the validity of a contest of an election, except that any member of the governing authority included in the contest shall disqualify himself from judging the contest.

- 4. Appeal. The final determination of the Mayor and Council may be appealed to the Superior Court of the County in the manner of appeal from a court of probate except that such appeal shall be made within ten (10) days after determination of the contest by the Mayor and Council.

2-502 Procedure for removal. Removal of any elected officer from C-) office shall be brought about in the following manner: N l.

Initiation of proceedings. Any person desiring to Initiate removal proceedings against an elected officer shall file a complaint in writing with the city clerk, which complaint shall set forth distinctly the alleged ground or grounds for removal and the names of witnesses, if any.

Preliminary hearing. Immediately upon receipt of a complaint as provided for in the preceding subsection, the city clerk shall notify the mayor (except in case of his. own impeachment, when the clerk shall then notify . the mayor pro tem.) who shall call a meeting of the city council. If, at such meeting, a majority of the council shall deem the complaint sufficient to author~

’ ize an investigation, they shall call, at the earliest date practicable, a meeting for the trial of the officer complained of.

Articles of impeachment and notice. If a trial is ordered as provided in the preceding subsection, it shall be the duty of the city attorney to immediately draw articles of impeachment, based upon the com- Plaint, which shall be filed with the city clerk at least five days prior to the date set for the trial. Upon receipt of the articles of impeachment it shall be the duty of the city clerk to attach to the same a notice directed to the party complained against, which notice shall specify the time and place of the trial and command the appearance of the accused. The notice and copy shall be. served upon the accused by a police officer at least seven days before the date of trial.

Conduct of trial. The trial shall be conducted in the manner employed by the courts, both the council and the accused having the right to introduce evidence and be represented by counsel, it being the duty of the city attorney to act as prosecuting officer in such trials.

Verdict and judgment. The Council shall render a verdict upon each article of impeachment, to be followed by the judgment, which shall be entered by the city attorney upon the original articles and signed by the mayor or other presiding officer. Such verdict and judgment shall be spread upon the minutes of the Council.

2-503 Appeal of decisions.

Any officer removed from office by the action of city council as provided in the preceding section shall have the right of appeal from the decision of the council to the Superior Court of the County in which city hall is located. Such appeal shall be governed by the same rules as govern appeals to the superior court from the court of probate. ,
